title: Manchester Art Gallery: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings that make activity—and its interruption—visible.
introduction:
The excavation in Ford Madox Brown’s *Work* forces different people into relation. Some dig, others watch or pass, and the street ceases to be a simple route from one place to another. This selection follows that distinction between taking part and standing aside. A shepherd neglects his animals, a family composes a reply to someone overseas, and a woman’s needlework receives the concentrated light often reserved for a public event.

The landscapes extend the question beyond individual bodies. Manchester appears at a distance from greener ground; rivers and fields accommodate trade and labour. These are different arrangements of social life, not illustrations of one uniform moral.
visitNote: This is a selection from Manchester Art Gallery’s collection, not a guaranteed sequence of displayed rooms. Works can be on loan or in storage. Check the gallery’s current programme and collection information before planning a visit around an individual painting.

books.title: The Elements of Drawing
books.author: John Ruskin
books.note: Ruskin’s attention to close observation accompanies the Pre-Raphaelite works and several studies of plants and ordinary materials. His exercises offer a way of examining their details without treating every object as a symbol.

works.title: Work
works.credit: Ford Madox Brown. Work. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The men digging occupy the street’s centre, while other classes and activities gather around the interruption. Brown gives labour a position that passers-by cannot simply ignore. The picture’s social argument is inseparable from its congestion: who works, who has time to watch, and who can move on must be read through their placement.

works.title: The Hireling Shepherd
works.credit: William Holman Hunt. The Hireling Shepherd. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The shepherd’s attention follows the woman while the sheep spread behind them. That divided field makes neglect more than an accusation supplied by the title. The foreground encounter has consequences elsewhere in the picture. Hunt asks the spectator to attend to both at once, rather than allowing the close pair to absorb every part of the scene.

works.title: Hylas and the Nymphs
works.credit: John William Waterhouse. Hylas and the Nymphs. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Hylas bends toward the women at the pool, and their reaching hands draw him across a boundary. Pale faces and shoulders are set against dark water, making the apparent invitation especially clear. The myth supplies its danger. The image holds attraction and risk together at the edge where land no longer offers secure footing.

works.title: Cheetah with Two Indian Servants and a Stag
works.catalogueTitle: Cheetah with Two Indian Servants and a Stag
works.credit: George Stubbs. Cheetah with Two Indian Servants and a Stag. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The attendants’ coordinated actions make the cheetah’s presence a managed situation. One gestures toward the distant stag, connecting animal observation to the staging of a hunt. Their work should remain visible within a picture often approached principally for Stubbs’s animals: the encounter depends on human handling as well as the anatomy of the cat.

works.title: The Dreamer
works.credit: Annie Swynnerton. The Dreamer. Image credit: Annie Swynnerton; Source credit: https://manchesterartgallery.org/explore/title/?mag-object-4412. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The small object and thread suggest an interrupted task, while the woman’s face remains directly present. The title invites an inward reading without supplying the thought. Swynnerton leaves those two conditions together: someone occupied with work, and someone whose attention cannot be fully explained by the visible materials in her hands.

works.title: Italian Girl with Necklace
works.credit: Susan Isabel Dacre. Italian Girl with Necklace. Image credit: Susan Isabel Dacre; Source credit: figurationfeminine. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The red necklace provides a clear accent against green surroundings and the young woman’s shoulder. Leaves frame the turned head without becoming a separate landscape. The portrait’s economy lies in this limited set of relations: a face, a few adjacent materials and colours strong enough to distinguish them without elaborate scenery.

works.title: Balaclava
works.credit: Elizabeth Thompson. Balaclava. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The men and horses no longer form a charge. Standing, sitting, exhausted and supported bodies break the group into separate conditions after combat. The comparatively quiet sky offers no equivalent of their disorder. Thompson places military action in its aftermath, where survival and fatigue replace the simple forward direction of an attack.

works.title: Feeding the Ducks
works.credit: Edward Stott. Feeding the Ducks. Image credit: Edward Stott; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The bowl joins the girl’s lowered attention to the approaching ducks. A small exchange becomes sufficient to organise the water’s edge, tree and reflections around it. There is no need for a dramatic gesture: the birds’ gathering supplies a response to the figure’s task and gives the quiet scene its action.

works.title: Ophelia
works.credit: Arthur Hughes. Ophelia. Image credit: Arthur Hughes; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The arched upper edge helps enclose a seated Ophelia within plants beside the water. Her raised hand and pale dress keep attention on a suspended bodily position. This is not the floating corpse familiar from Millais. Hughes holds the figure on the bank, leaving the event associated with her name outside the depicted moment.

works.title: The Death of Arthur
works.credit: James Archer. La mort d'Arthur. Image credit: James Archer; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The armoured body requires attendance from the surrounding women. Their positions organise a scene in which the principal figure can no longer act. Beyond them, the waiting boat gives the shore a direction of departure. The legend’s ending is presented through care for a body and preparation for what happens next.

works.title: Girl Reading
works.credit: Charles Edward Perugini. Girl Reading. Image credit: Charles Edward Perugini; Source credit: https://manchesterartgallery.org/explore/title/?mag-object-734. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The open book remains on the lap while one hand supports the chin. Reading is present, but so is the bodily pause around it. Dark foliage makes the pale figure clear without supplying an explanation for her thoughts. Perugini gives an ordinary adjustment of posture enough attention to become the picture’s main event.

works.title: Answering the Emigrant’s Letter
works.credit: James Collinson. Answering the Emigrant's Letter. Image credit: James Collinson; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The emigrant is absent, but the letter gathers a household around the work of replying. Different people share a table and attend to one sheet. Distance is therefore made visible through its effect on those who remain at home: communication becomes a collective effort rather than a private exchange between two isolated individuals.

works.title: A Bunch of Thistles
works.credit: Rose Magnus. A Bunch of Thistles. Image credit: Rose Magnus; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The thistles retain their pointed leaves and uneven heads rather than being smoothed into an ideal bouquet. A simple vessel and plain ground leave that irregularity room. The painting’s structure follows the plant’s difficult outlines, giving something prickly and commonplace the sustained attention usually associated with more accommodating flowers.

works.title: Gathering Plums
works.credit: Henry Herbert La Thangue. Gathering Plums. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: One figure bends close to the ground while another continues the harvest farther back. Repeated changes of posture connect the foreground task to a larger area beneath the trees. The basket gives the labour a practical destination, keeping the sunlit scene attached to the effort of gathering rather than mere enjoyment of the orchard.

works.title: Chelsea Regatta
works.credit: Walter Greaves. Chelsea Regatta. Image credit: Walter Greaves; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Boats, shore and buildings offer different positions from which to participate in the regatta. No single spectator accounts for its scale. Greaves accumulates small incidents around the shared river, allowing the event to spread across places occupied in different ways instead of reducing it to one decisive boat race.

works.title: Manchester from Belle Vue
works.credit: George Danson. Manchester from Belle Vue. Image credit: George Danson; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Factories and smoke belong to the distant city, with people and animals on greener ground nearer the spectator. The separation makes urban growth a relationship between environments rather than a view composed only of buildings. Distance does important work: it permits the industrial area to be seen as an extent within a larger landscape.

works.title: View of Manchester from Kersal
works.credit: John Barton Waddington. View of Manchester from Kersal. Image credit: John Barton Waddington; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The elevated position gives an account of Manchester’s spread along the river. Chimneys and large buildings emerge through haze beyond comparatively open ground. That foreground is a measure as well as a setting: the city’s occupation of the distant landscape becomes more legible because the near land is less densely built.

works.title: Sweet Industry
works.credit: Laura Theresa Alma-Tadema. Sweet Industry. Image credit: Laura Theresa Alma-Tadema; Source credit: Manchester Art Gallery , image. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The illuminated hands and needlework give the dark room a small working centre. The woman’s pink dress remains part of that contained situation rather than a public display. Alma-Tadema allows skill to appear through concentration and a limited gesture, without expanding the domestic task into a theatrical performance.

works.title: Grapes
works.credit: William Jabez Muckley. Grapes. Image credit: William Jabez Muckley; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Glass, grapes, fabric and the patterned dish are packed closely, yet each remains distinguishable. Reflections and changes in translucency do work that wider gaps might otherwise perform. Muckley makes material differences the still life’s organising principle: the same light cannot produce the same surface on every object.

works.title: Berengaria’s Alarm for the Safety of Richard I
works.catalogueTitle: Berengaria's Alarm for the Safety of Her Husband, Richard Coeur de Lion, Awakened by the Sight of His Girdle Offered for Sale at Rome
works.credit: Charles Allston Collins. Berengaria's Alarm for the Safety of Her Husband, Richard Coeur de Lion, Awakened by the Sight of His Girdle Offered for Sale at Rome. Image credit: Charles Allston Collins; Source credit: scan of painting. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The visitor’s displayed object changes how people attend to one another. Berengaria rises, and the surrounding figures turn toward the exchange. The historical narrative reaches the room through something small enough to be shown in a hand. Recognition is distributed through gestures before it becomes a fully stated account of the news.

closingSections.title: Begin with a kind of attention
paragraphs: *Work*, *Sweet Industry* and *Answering the Emigrant’s Letter* make a useful trio: public labour, domestic skill and the work of maintaining a distant relationship. Compare how each gives its task a centre. This selection includes collection holdings rather than a confirmed hanging; consult the gallery for current availability.
